title: Section 81 — Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage

content.overview: BNS s. 81 — Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage. BNS restatement of IPC 493. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 493. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 81 is the rule on “Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage”. The section provides that every man who by deceit causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 81 exists so that “Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

learningObjectives: Master the ingredients of deceitfully inducing a woman into cohabitation or sexual intercourse under belief of marriage.
Differentiate s. 81 from s. 69 (deceitful promise of marriage) and s. 63 (rape).
Understand the requirement of actual deceit regarding the legal status of an existing marriage.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 81 penalizes any man who, by deceit, causes any woman who is not lawfully married to him to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit or have sexual intercourse with him in that belief, punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminal law protects women from fraudulent matrimonial deception where a man intentionally orchestrates a sham marital status to induce cohabitation or sexual relations.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 81 (corresponding to IPC s. 493).
Substantive act: Man causing a woman not lawfully married to him to believe by deceit that she is lawfully married to him.
Consequential act: Inducing cohabitation or sexual intercourse in reliance on that fraudulent belief.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to ten years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused is a man and the complainant is a woman not lawfully married to him.
The man practiced deceit upon the woman.
The deceit induced the woman to believe that she was lawfully married to him.
Under that induced belief, the woman cohabited or had sexual intercourse with the man.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 81 addresses the grave moral and bodily fraud where an unmarried man, or a married man, induces a woman to believe that a lawful marriage has already been solemnized between them. The core of the offence is deceit regarding the existence of a valid lawful marriage (e.g., executing fake wedding ceremonies, forging official marriage certificates, or lying about customs having legal force). Under this induced false belief of lawful marriage, the woman consents to cohabitation or sexual relations. Section 81 is distinguished from rape because the woman's consent to intercourse was ostensibly given, but vitiated by deceit regarding the marital bond itself.
examples: Teaching example (Fake marriage ceremony): An accused hires an actor dressed as a priest, performs a bogus private ritual in a hotel room, and tells the woman that they are now legally husband and wife under statutory law. Relying on this belief, she cohabits with him. The accused is liable under s. 81.

Teaching example (Future promise vs existing belief): A man promises to marry a woman next year and engages in consensual intercourse on that promise. Section 81 does not apply because she knew she was not yet married; the matter falls under s. 69 (deceitful promise to marry).
distinctions: Section 81 vs Section 69: Section 81 requires inducing a belief that a lawful marriage already exists; Section 69 penalizes intercourse obtained on a false promise of future marriage or other deceitful means.

Section 81 vs Section 83: Section 83 penalizes fraudulently going through a ceremony of marriage without lawful marriage; Section 81 requires the subsequent consequence of cohabitation or sexual intercourse.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who presented a forged marriage registration certificate to a woman and subsequently resided with her as husband and wife is guilty under s. 81.
Rule: Inducing a false belief of existing lawful marriage through deceitful documents followed by cohabitation satisfies all elements of BNS s. 81.
Application: The woman genuinely believed the registration was genuine and cohabited solely on that foundation.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 81.

Must be followed by cohabitation or sexual intercourse.
Distinct from future promise to marry under s. 69.
Punishable with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
